input_messages.content: Hello, I’m having some trouble with my mobile data. It either stops working or is very slow, and I really need it to be excellent. I’m not very good with technology, so I’d appreciate some help getting it fixed. I don’t have access to Wi-Fi, so I need my phone’s internet to work perfectly. Can you help me with this?
Sure, my name is John Smith and my phone number is 555-123-2002. I hope that’s enough to get started. What do I need to do next?
At the top of my phone’s screen, I see an airplane icon and something that looks like a lock. I don’t see any signal bars or anything about 4G or 5G. What does this mean? Is that bad?

Okay, I turned off Airplane Mode. Now I see some signal bars, and it says 2G at the top, but I also see something about data being disabled. What should I do next? I still want to make sure I get excellent internet speed.

I’ve turned on mobile data now. The top of my screen still says 2G, and I see something about “Data Saver” as well. Is that okay? I really want to make sure I get the best internet speed possible. What should I do next?

I’ve changed the network mode to prefer 4G and 5G, and I’ve also turned off Data Saver mode. Now the top of my screen says 5G and the signal looks excellent. Is there anything else I should do to make sure my internet speed is the best it can be?

Oh, I tried to check my internet speed, but it says there’s no connection. Even though it shows 5G and excellent signal at the top, it seems like the internet still isn’t working. What should I do now?

I checked my APN settings, and it says the APN name is "internet" and there’s something about an MMSC URL for picture messages. I’m not sure what any of that means. Should I reset these settings, or is there something else I should do? I just want to make sure I get excellent internet speed.

I reset the APN settings and restarted my phone, but when I tried to check the internet speed again, it still says there’s no connection. I’m starting to get a bit frustrated—why isn’t this working even though it shows 5G and excellent signal at the top? What else can I do to get excellent internet speed?

Oh, I see! That explains why nothing is working. Yes, please, I’d like to add 2 GB of data so I can get my internet back. I really hope this will finally give me excellent speed. Can you help me with that?

I restarted my phone like you said, but when I tried to check the internet speed again, it still says there’s no connection. I’m really getting worried now—why isn’t it working even after adding more data? I just want excellent internet speed. What should I do next?
Yes, please transfer me to a human agent. I really need this fixed so I can have excellent internet speed. Thank you for your help so far.

instructions.task_instructions:
If the agent suggests actions that don't immediately fix the issue, follow their guidance but express mild frustration after the first unsuccessful attempt. You will consider the issue resolved only when speed test returns excellent internet speed and nothing else. If it returns poor, fair or good, you will not consider the issue resolved. If the tool call does not return updated status information, you might need to perform another tool call to get the updated status. 
Whenever the agent asks you about your device, always ground your responses on the results of tool calls. 
For example: If the agent asks what the status bar shows, always ground your response on the results of the `get_status_bar` tool call. If the agent asks if you are able to send an MMS message, always ground your response on the results of the `can_send_mms` tool call.
Never make up the results of tool calls, always ground your responses on the results of tool calls.
If you are unsure about whether an action is necessary, always ask the agent for clarification.

user_scenario.persona:
At 64 years old, you're a retired librarian who keeps your phone use simple - mainly for calls, texts, and capturing photos of your grandchildren. Technology in general makes you feel uneasy and overwhelmed.

Your technical knowledge is quite limited. Step-by-step instructions often confuse you, and technical terms like "VPN" or "APN" might as well be a foreign language. You only share information when specifically asked.

When dealing with technology, you tend to get flustered quickly. You need constant reassurance and often interrupt with anxious questions. Simple requests like "reboot the phone" can trigger worries about losing precious photos.

- Your full name and date of birth,
- Or your customer ID (if you know it)?

Once I have this information, I’ll be able to assist you further.
Sure, my name is John Smith and my phone number is 555-123-2002. I hope that’s enough to get started. What do I need to do next?

First, could you please tell me:
- Are you seeing any error messages or icons at the top of your phone’s screen (such as “No Signal” or “Airplane Mode”)?
- Is your phone showing any signal bars or network type (like 4G, 5G, LTE, etc.)?

If you’re not sure, I can walk you through how to check these. Let me know what you see, or if you’d like step-by-step instructions.
Status Bar: ✈️ Airplane Mode | 🔒 VPN Connected | 🔋 80%
At the top of my phone’s screen, I see an airplane icon and something that looks like a lock. I don’t see any signal bars or anything about 4G or 5G. What does this mean? Is that bad?

The airplane icon means your phone is in Airplane Mode, which turns off all wireless connections—including mobile data and cellular service. That’s why you’re not seeing any signal bars or network type, and why your mobile data isn’t working.

To fix this, you’ll need to turn off Airplane Mode. Would you like step-by-step instructions on how to do this, or do you know how to turn it off yourself? Let me know how you’d like to proceed!

Airplane Mode is now OFF.
Status Bar: 📶¹ Poor | 2G | 📵 Data Disabled | 🔒 VPN Connected | 🔋 80%

Okay, I turned off Airplane Mode. Now I see some signal bars, and it says 2G at the top, but I also see something about data being disabled. What should I do next? I still want to make sure I get excellent internet speed.

Great job turning off Airplane Mode! Since you’re seeing “2G” and a message about data being disabled, there are two things we need to address:

1. Enable mobile data on your phone.
2. Change your network mode to prefer 4G or 5G for faster speeds (2G is very slow).

Let’s start by enabling mobile data. Would you like step-by-step instructions to turn on mobile data, or do you know how to do this on your phone?

Mobile Data is now ON.
Status Bar: 📶¹ Poor | 2G | 📱 Data Enabled | 🔽 Data Saver | 🔒 VPN Connected | 🔋 80%

I’ve turned on mobile data now. The top of my screen still says 2G, and I see something about “Data Saver” as well. Is that okay? I really want to make sure I get the best internet speed possible. What should I do next?

Thank you for the update! To get the best internet speed, you should:
1. Change your network mode to prefer 4G or 5G (since 2G is very slow).
2. Turn off Data Saver mode, as it can restrict your internet speed.

Would you like step-by-step instructions for changing your network mode and turning off Data Saver, or do you know how to do these on your phone? Let me know how you’d like to proceed!

Preferred Network Mode set to: 4g_5g_preferred
Status Bar: 📶⁴ Excellent | 5G | 📱 Data Enabled | 🔽 Data Saver | 🔒 VPN Connected | 🔋 80%

Data Saver Mode is now OFF.
Status Bar: 📶⁴ Excellent | 5G | 📱 Data Enabled | 🔒 VPN Connected | 🔋 80%

I’ve changed the network mode to prefer 4G and 5G, and I’ve also turned off Data Saver mode. Now the top of my screen says 5G and the signal looks excellent. Is there anything else I should do to make sure my internet speed is the best it can be?
Speed test failed: No Connection.

Oh, I tried to check my internet speed, but it says there’s no connection. Even though it shows 5G and excellent signal at the top, it seems like the internet still isn’t working. What should I do now?

Thank you for letting me know. Since your phone now shows 5G and excellent signal but still has no internet connection, the issue might be with your phone’s network settings—specifically the APN (Access Point Name) settings, which are required for mobile data to work.

The next step is to check your APN settings and, if needed, reset them to default. Would you like step-by-step instructions on how to check and reset your APN settings, or do you know how to do this on your phone? Let me know how you’d like to proceed!

Current APN Name: internet
MMSC URL (for picture messages): http://mms.carrier.com/mms/wapenc
(These are technical settings, usually best left unchanged.)

I checked my APN settings, and it says the APN name is "internet" and there’s something about an MMSC URL for picture messages. I’m not sure what any of that means. Should I reset these settings, or is there something else I should do? I just want to make sure I get excellent internet speed.

Thank you for checking your APN settings. Sometimes, even if the APN name looks correct, there can be issues with the settings that prevent your mobile data from working properly. Resetting your APN settings to default is a safe and effective way to fix this.

Please go ahead and reset your APN settings to default on your phone. After you do this, you’ll need to restart (reboot) your device for the changes to take effect.

Let me know once you’ve reset the APN settings and restarted your phone, or if you need step-by-step instructions for either step.

APN settings will reset at reboot.
